newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends at new low vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends at new low vs dollar.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee again ended at an all-time low of 56.90 to the dollar on Thursday as seasonal import covering drove the U.S. currency up, dealers said.
This compares with the rupee's previous record low of 56.85 set on Wednesday.
"There was big demand from a public sector bank and a foreign bank who were buying dollars to cover trade-backed transactions," a Standard Chartered Bank dealer said.
He said the last quarter of a year traditionally sees heavy demand for the dollar as imports rise to meet holiday season demands.
The Central Bank pushed the dollar up by 3.75 local cents in the morning, setting buying and selling rates at 55.8979 and 56.0271 respectively.
A Commercial Bank dealer said the supply of dollars in the local market was limited with banks holding on to their positions, anticipating a further decline of the rupee.
"The dollar is also fairly bullish these days in overseas markets, which contributes to its strength locally," he said.
The overnight call money, which opened at 15.74, closed at 18 percent.
